drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna need to state 'שהיוצא מן הטמא טמא'?
outcomeNote: the question is answered in the following unit

segments.he: וּמָה הֵן בַּאֲכִילָה כּוּ׳. לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנֵי ״שֶׁהַיּוֹצֵא״?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches with regard to an animal whose offspring resembles a different species: «And what» is the offspring’s halakhic status «with regard to» its «consumption?» In the case of a kosher animal that gave birth to a non-kosher animal of sorts, its consumption is permitted. And in the case of a non-kosher animal that gave birth to a kosher animal of sorts, its consumption is prohibited. This is because that which emerges from the non-kosher animal is non-kosher and that which emerges from the kosher animal is kosher. The Gemara asks: «Why do I» need the mishna «to teach» the concluding phrase: This is «because that which emerges» from the non-kosher animal is non-kosher and that which emerges from the kosher animal is kosher?
